A step-by-step guide on how to configure Apple Time Machine to back up over an SMB network share using a sparse bundle virtual disk image.
1. Create a Sparse Image (Virtual Disk) There are two ways to create this virtual disk: via commands in the terminal, or using macOS Disk Utility.
Option A: Using the Terminal Navigate to the directory where you want to create the initial virtual disk (work locally first, not directly on the SMB share):
cd ~/Desktop Run the following command to create a 500GB virtual disk image named TimeMachine. Adjust the size to suit your needs (roughly 1.5x to 2x your Mac’s storage capacity is recommended):
hdiutil create -size 500g -type SPARSEBUNDLE -fs "HFS+J" TimeMachine.sparsebundle Option B: Using Disk Utility (GUI) Open Disk Utility. Click File > New Image > Blank Image… in the menu bar, or press ⌘ + N. Set Image Format to “sparse bundle disk image”. Set the desired maximum size (select the format first to prevent size reset errors). Name the disk (e.g., TimeMachine) and optionally enable encryption. Set the save location to your Desktop and click Save. 2. Copy the Image File to Your Network Share Open Finder and navigate to the network SMB share you want to use for backups. Drag the TimeMachine.sparsebundle file you just created into this folder.
Once the copy has finished completely, you can delete the local copy from your Desktop. Now double-click the sparse bundle on your network share to mount it. You should see the mounted TimeMachine volume appear in Finder’s sidebar.
3. Add the Image as a Destination for Time Machine Because the macOS Time Machine settings UI typically does not allow directly selecting mounted network sparse bundles, register it as a destination via the terminal:
sudo tmutil setdestination /Volumes/TimeMachine (If you chose a different volume name, adjust /Volumes/TimeMachine accordingly.)
4. Mount the Image Automatically on Login Since macOS does not automatically remount network sparse bundles after a reboot, a small AppleScript app handles mounting on startup:
Open Script Editor (located in /Applications/Utilities). Paste the following script, replacing the share path and image name with your actual values: tell application "Finder" try mount volume "smb://your-nas-ip-or-hostname/share-name" delay 5 do shell script "hdiutil attach /Volumes/share-name/TimeMachine.sparsebundle" end try end tell Save the script as an Application (e.g. MountTimeMachine.app). Go to System Settings > General > Login Items (or System Preferences > Users & Groups > Login Items) and add your new application to the list. Now every time you log in, your Mac will automatically mount the backup image, allowing Time Machine to run without manual intervention.
summary: A step-by-step guide on how to configure Apple Time Machine to back up over an SMB network share using a sparse bundle virtual disk image.
title: Making a Mac Time Machine Backup on an SMB Share

Hi everyone, this is basically a guest post. This guide was written by TimLew — huge shoutout to him! 💖
Discord: timlew
Step 1: Download the ISO File Download Link: Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 (x64) ISO
Note: This is the standard Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC ISO (non-IoT), which keeps your system language as German. The IoT conversion is handled during installation.
Step 2: Verify System Language Open PowerShell as Administrator. Run: dism /english /online /get-intl | find /i "Default system UI language" If the output confirms German (de-DE), proceed to the next step.
If not, download the matching language ISO from: Windows LTSC Download Links
Step 3: Back Up Your Data ⚠️ Back up all critical files from your C: drive (bookmarks, documents, passwords, photos, etc.).
Note: While the in-place upgrade process is generally smooth, it technically transitions the build version from 22H2 to 21H2. Backing up first is always strongly advised.
Step 4: Modify the Registry Key In PowerShell (Admin), run:
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion" /v EditionID /d IoTEnterpriseS /f Immediately mount the downloaded ISO and launch setup.exe.
Step 5: Perform the Upgrade During setup, select “Keep personal files and apps”.
⚠️ Important: Act quickly — Windows may revert the registry value if you wait too long before starting setup!
Allow the installation to complete.
Step 6: Activate IoT Enterprise LTSC After the upgrade completes, use the generic Windows setup key:
QPM6N-7J2WJ-P88HH-P3YRH-YY74H Your system may restart automatically.
Step 7: System Activation Open PowerShell (Admin) and run the Microsoft Activation Script:
irm https://get.activated.win | iex Select Option [1] (HWID activation).
Step 8: Restore Microsoft Store (Optional) If the Microsoft Store is missing after the upgrade and you need it, run in PowerShell (Admin):
wsreset -i Wait 1–2 minutes for the Store to reinstall in the background. If any warnings appear in the terminal, you can safely ignore them.
To install App Installer / WinGet (if needed): Download App Installer from Microsoft Store
The Microsoft Store must be installed for this link to open.
✅ Done! Your system is now running Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC with extended support.

A curated collection of interesting tools, services, guides, and resources that I’ve found useful or noteworthy.
Archiving RedditToMarkDown - Save Reddit threads as Markdown files. Useful before mods remove posts or Reddit changes access rules. Pandoc - Convert between different markup languages (e.g. HTML <-> Markdown). Ente - Open-source, end-to-end encrypted alternative to Google Photos; also includes an authenticator app. Use my referral code to get 10GB extra storage: DKSCPX Development SVG Tutorial - Learn how to code vector graphics in HTML with SVG. Fonts Commit Mono - A neutral, highly legible monospaced font engineered for programmers. Departure Mono - A monospaced pixel font with a lo-fi, techy vibe. Geist - A typeface specifically designed for developers and designers. PDF Stirling-PDF - Powerful, locally hosted web application for PDF manipulation (merge, split, convert, OCR). BentoPDF - Web-based PDF editor and viewer. (GitHub) Privacy JustDeleteMe - Directory of direct links and instructions for deleting accounts from web services. LocalSend - Open-source, cross-platform local network file sharing (AirDrop alternative) that works completely offline without accounts or external servers. Torrenting awesome-german-piracy - A curated list of (not only) German indexing and sharing sites. German Torrents - Overview of German torrent trackers and indexing sites. Screensharing Pin.gl - Ultra-low-latency screen and camera sharing (browser-based). Screego - Web-based screen sharing. (GitHub) Utilities IT-Tools - Handy collection of web-based developer and sysadmin utilities (GitHub). Dev-Toys - A collection of developer tools. Just as above but as a desktop app. (GitHub) Misc Excalidraw - Virtual whiteboard for sketching hand-drawn diagrams. Supports real-time collaboration with others. Great for quick system sketches and architecture notes. FossFlow - A tool to design isometric infrastructure diagrams (GitHub). 4get - A privacy-focused proxy search engine that doesn’t track or filter results. SmallDocs - A web-based Markdown editor with clean export and styling options. Spotube - Open-source Spotify client that doesn’t require Premium or use Electron. Available for desktop & mobile. I’ve donated to this project, by the way! ❤️ Website themes with uBlock Origin - Guide to injecting custom CSS themes into websites using uBlock Origin. Displaying Website Content on an E-Ink Display - Write-up on rendering web content on low-power E-Ink screens.
summary: A curated collection of interesting tools, services, guides, and resources that I’ve found useful or noteworthy.
title: List of Interesting Things

Hey everyone! This is a short guide on how to download the portable version of ClamAV for Windows and run a quick scan on your system.
1. Download ClamAV (Portable / No Install) First, visit the ClamAV GitHub Releases page and download the latest Windows .zip release. Extract the contents of the ZIP archive to a folder of your choice.
2. Download the ClamAV Databases Before scanning, you need to configure freshclam.exe to download signature databases:
Navigate to the conf_examples folder. Copy the example configuration file (freshclam.conf.sample) into the main ClamAV directory and rename it to freshclam.conf. Open freshclam.conf in a text editor, remove or comment out the line that says Example, and configure the database directory path if desired. Now open a terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell), navigate to your ClamAV directory, and run:
freshclam.exe It will begin downloading the latest virus definition databases. After a few minutes, the update will finish.
3. Scan Your Entire System In the same terminal, run clamscan.exe with the recursive scanning flag and the target drive or folder:
clamscan.exe --recursive C:\ More Information For more information and advanced scanning options, take a look at the official ClamAV documentation.
summary: Hey everyone! This is a short guide on how to download the portable version of ClamAV for Windows and run a quick scan on your system.
title: Do a quick system scan with ClamAV
